# Implementation Plan: 1a-fork-doc — Codex fork strategy commit

*Generated by `/plan-with-ralph` on 2026-05-13. Ready for `/implement-with-ralph --from-plan .ralph/jobs/1a-fork-doc/plan.md`.*

## Overview

Phase 1a of the codexu roadmap commits the canonical *fork-strategy documentation* into the codex submodule and locks the decision in codexu. The strategy itself is already in effect (subtree mirror at `external/repos/codex-patched/`, overlay crates at `codex-rs-overlay/`, submodule pointer to `gim-home/codex`). This commit writes it down so future agents working in either repo find a single, internally consistent description and stop re-litigating.

This is a **documentation-only commit.** No Rust, no tests, no protocol changes. Three files inside the codex submodule (`docs/implementation/architecture.md`, `docs/implementation/patch-surface.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) get additive updates, then the codexu submodule pointer is bumped and `codexu-roadmap.md` records the decision under §"Decisions made".

The plan is split into TWO stories so the autonomously-verifiable part (US-001: local doc edits + local commit + diff surfaced) does not collide with the operator-gated part (US-002: push to `gim-home/codex` + pointer bump on codexu).

## Research Findings

### Codebase context
- `codex/` is a git submodule of codexu (`gim-home/codex` via HTTPS; confirmed in codexu's `.gitmodules`).
- Inside the codex submodule, upstream `openai/codex` lives as a **git subtree** mirrored at `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/` (subtree root). The Rust workspace inside is at `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/`. (The PRD's looser phrasing of "codex-rs/ is the subtree" is imprecise; the docs MUST use the strict phrasing.)
- Fork-only divergence work lives in `codex/codex-rs-overlay/` as overlay crates. Working precedents (confirmed present): `codex-copilot`, `codex-copilot-launcher`, `codex-invariant-tests`.
- The subtree workspace at `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/codex-rs/Cargo.toml` references overlay crates via relative paths like `../../../../codex-rs-overlay/codex-copilot`.

Plan DOES NOT modify this section.**

### Codexu-side consumer doc (read-only — `codexu/docs/plans/codex-fork-extension-strategy.md`)
Encodes 3 Gates for any future fork patch:
- Gate 1 — overlay-first design exploration (default placement = `codex-rs-overlay/`)
- Gate 2 — upstream churn data (<2 commits/month threshold per file)
- Gate 3 — patch registration (`// SANDBOX PATCH:` marker + `patch-surface.md` §14/§15 entry + invariant test in `codex-invariant-tests/`)

Cross-references from new codex-side docs to this consumer-side doc MUST use a plain-text path reference (e.g., "see the codexu repo's `docs/plans/codex-fork-extension-strategy.md`"), NOT a Markdown link — the path does not resolve when codex is cloned standalone.

### Technical constraints
- **DO NOT EDIT** anything under `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/` (upstream mirror) or `codex/codex-rs-overlay/` (overlay crates).
- **DO NOT EDIT** `codex/AGENTS.override.md` (tenets source of truth).
- **DO NOT EDIT** the §"Core engineering tenants" section in `codex/CLAUDE.md` (mirrors AGENTS.override.md; would diverge them).
- **DO NOT** silently close the open W-5 RFC in `codex/docs/plans/reduce-conflict-surface.md` (proposes converting `external/repos/codex-patched/` from subtree to submodule).
- **DO NOT** assert that codex IS a submodule unconditionally. Use conditional framing: "When consumed by codexu, codex/ is a git submodule...". The codex repo is also used standalone.
- **DO NOT** confuse the two layers: outer (codexu → codex via submodule) vs inner (codex → openai/codex via subtree, currently). Document as separate.
- **DO NOT** introduce wording that implies an RPC contract version is locked in this commit. This commit covers layout/placement strategy only.
- **DO NOT** write cross-repo references as Markdown links (`[text](codexu/docs/...)`); use prose pointers ("see the codexu repo's `docs/plans/...`").
- **DO NOT** stage unrelated dirty hunks in the codexu pointer-bump commit. Use the dedicated clean worktree (worktree #3).

## Approach

### Architecture
Three additive doc edits in the codex submodule + one parent-side commit in codexu. No code. The edits make the *implicit* fork strategy *explicit* and cross-link the codex-side and codexu-side strategy docs so future agents find a coherent contract from either entry point.

### Implementation strategy

Split into two stories so autonomous and operator-gated work do not collide.

## Scope

### In scope
- Three doc files inside the codex submodule (additive edits) — US-001.
- One doc file in codexu (`plans/codexu-roadmap.md` — new "Decisions made" entry + forward-pointer on "Decisions still open #1") — US-002.
- Codexu submodule pointer bump — US-002.
- A `1a-fork-doc-strategy` topic branch pushed to `gim-home/codex` (operator-gated push).
- A `1a-fork-doc-pointer-bump` topic branch on codexu (operator-gated push).

### Out of scope
- ANY code change (Rust, scripts, configs).
- ANY test addition.
- Editing `codex/external/repos/codex-patched/**` or `codex/codex-rs-overlay/**`.
- Editing `codex/AGENTS.override.md` (mirror source of truth — would diverge from CLAUDE.md tenets).
- Editing the §"Core engineering tenants" section of `codex/CLAUDE.md` (mirrors AGENTS.override.md).
- Resolving the W-5 RFC (subtree → submodule for inner layer).
- Locking a fixed cadence frequency for subtree pulls (procedural-only).
- RPC contract versioning (mentioned in roadmap Phase 1a as future work).
- Migrating content from `codexu/docs/plans/codex-fork-extension-strategy.md` into the codex submodule (it stays codexu-side; codex docs only point to it).
- Adding §14/§15 rows for the three Phase 2c/2d/7 patches (those land in their respective implementation PRs).
- Modifying anything in the dirty paths of the parent codexu working tree that isn't `plans/codexu-roadmap.md` or the submodule pointer (`packages/happy-agent/dist/*` and other unrelated dirty paths must stay unstaged).

## Operator choices

Three viable framings were surfaced during research. Defaults are chosen below; the implementer must re-surface each at step 6 before the codex commit lands if anything looks off.

| Choice | Default (chosen) | Alternative considered | Decision rationale |
|--------|------------------|------------------------|--------------------|
| architecture.md placement of "Fork strategy" | New top-level § between "Solution" and "Traffic flow" | Subsection under "Solution" | Architect + Codex agreed: fork strategy is foundational architectural context, deserves peer-level emphasis. |
| patch-surface.md schema for upcoming patches | New §17 "Upcoming roadmap-owned seams" subsection (lightweight, advisory) | Extend §14 with a Status column + 3 rows | Codex + Copilot preferred a separate section to preserve §14's shipped-invariants registry semantics. Copilot's High-severity concern about the registry-pollution risk is mitigated by §17 being explicitly "advisory only, not part of the shipped inventory" and by keeping it compact. |
| Subtree pull cadence | Procedural-shape-only (stable tag + lag-check + operator-gated frequency); defer fixed cadence | Lock quarterly OR lock opportunistic-only | The PRD does not require cadence selection; defaulting to a frequency without operational data risks needing revision. |
| Disposition of `Decisions still open #1` in codexu-roadmap.md after the "Decisions made" entry lands | Add forward-pointer line "RESOLVED 2026-05-13" at top of the open entry; preserve the original entry below for history | Delete or strikethrough | Architect + Codex flagged this as small but real; preserving history is the conservative pick. Resurface at step 6 if operator wants the original entry removed. |
| Push approach (codex side) | Defer to operator at step 8 | n/a | Cannot be defaulted — affects gim-home/codex remote state. |
| Push approach (codexu side) | Defer to operator at step 13 | n/a | Cannot be defaulted — affects codexu main. |

## Risk areas

1. **Silent contradiction between codex-side and codexu-side docs over time.** Mitigation: each new section names the authoritative source for that rule (Gates 1–3 → codexu side; layout details → codex side); cross-refs use prose pointers so a future agent must consciously look up the other side.
2. **Future Phase 2c/2d/7 patches landing without §14/§15 entries.** Mitigation: §17 closing sentence explicitly states unregistered patches may be silently dropped on the next rebase.
3. **Implementer accidentally documenting the W-5 subtree→submodule outcome.** Mitigation: explicit non-preemption sentence in architecture.md.
4. **Implementer accidentally including unrelated dirty paths in the codexu pointer-bump commit.** Mitigation: dedicated clean US-002 worktree; `git diff --cached --stat` before commit; operator review.
5. **CLAUDE.md tenets section drift from AGENTS.override.md.** Mitigation: plan explicitly DOES NOT edit the tenets section in CLAUDE.md; only the Consumer-codexu section. Acceptance criterion verifies the tenets section is unchanged.
6. **Cross-repo links resolving to dead paths when codex is cloned standalone.** Mitigation: use prose pointers ("the codexu repo's `docs/plans/...`") rather than markdown links.
7. **Codexu pointer bumped to a topic-branch-only commit that's not on `gim-home/codex` `main`.** Mitigation: hard gate at end of step 8 — `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main` must pass before step 9.
8. **Operator review at step 6 misses an issue and commit-message must be amended.** Mitigation: review is before commit creation; commit is created only after operator approves (or autonomous defaults are accepted).
9. **patch-surface.md §17 insertion at the wrong line.** Mitigation: explicit insertion-point spec — between close of §16 (~L968) and start of duplicate-§11 appendix (~L971). Internal-consistency check at step 5 confirms `grep "17\. Upcoming roadmap-owned seams"` returns exactly one match.
10. **architecture.md TOC not updated.** Mitigation: explicit step 2 sub-bullet + AC that grep finds "Fork strategy" in BOTH the TOC and as a top-level heading.

## Preliminary Story Decomposition

- **US-001 (small):** Set up codex worktree → edit 3 codex docs → internal-consistency check → operator-review the diff → commit on topic branch. Fully autonomously verifiable apart from the operator-review pause.
- **US-002 (small):** Operator-gated push to gim-home/codex → wait for `origin/main` reachability gate → clean codexu pointer-bump worktree → bump submodule + add roadmap entry → operator-gated push of codexu commit → cleanup.

The split decouples the autonomously-checkable doc work (US-001) from the operator-state-changing actions (US-002), so US-001 can land deterministically and US-002 can be paused on operator availability without rolling back US-001.

## Open Questions
1. **Cadence frequency locking** — deferred. Revisit once a real subtree pull has happened on the locked-strategy infrastructure (likely after the first Phase 2c/2d patch).
2. **PR vs fast-forward on gim-home/codex** — operator picks at push time (US-002 step 8). Plan does not prescribe.
3. **PR vs fast-forward on codexu** — operator picks at push time (US-002 step 13). Plan does not prescribe.
4. **Whether to keep the original §"Decisions still open #1" text or strikethrough it** — default: keep with forward-pointer. Revisit at step 6 if operator wants it removed.
5. **Whether AGENTS.override.md or CLAUDE.md should be the canonical for the tenets** — out of scope for Phase 1a; the plan deliberately edits neither side of the mirrored section. If future work decides one is canonical, that's a separate doc-consistency PR.
